title: The Housing Authority: audit findings and inspection scores, year by year
question: What have the Housing Authority’s own auditors and the federal inspectors reported, year by year?
finding: The Authority’s audits reported findings on its federal programs in 7 of the 7 years from 2019 to 2025: 22 findings, 19 of them marked as repeats of an earlier year, while the federal money it spent rose from $330.0 million to $525.6 million. Findings fell from 5 in 2019 to 2 in 2025. Federal inspectors scored its public-housing developments 38 times in the files on disk; 15 of those scores were below 60 out of 100, and the number of developments inspected fell from 23 in the busiest year to 1 in 2025 as buildings left the public-housing program.
how: Audit rows are taken from this project’s the site’s “Audits and official documents” page (screen "public-body-audit-findings"), which reads every audit the Authority filed with the Federal Audit Clearinghouse; a finding is counted once per audit and reference number. Inspection rows count the federal physical-inspection scores of the Authority’s public-housing developments by the year of inspection, across every vintage of the federal file on disk, each inspection once.
limits: An audit tests a sample of federal programs, so few findings can mean good controls or a narrow sample; a repeat finding means the auditor judged last year’s problem not yet fixed. Inspection files list only the latest inspections at each release, and three vintages are missing, so years are uneven. The Authority is a separate public body; the City does not run it. The audit reports themselves, linked in each row, say what each finding was.
